network_resize_interpolation: torchvision.transforms.Resize on PIL input; bilinear default

grad_cam.target_layer: model.layer4[-1].conv2 (second convolution of the final ResNet-18 BasicBlock)
grad_cam.target_class_rule: argmax predicted class on the unperturbed normalized image; same class held fixed for every perturbation
grad_cam.activation_map_postprocess: ReLU; bilinear upsample to 224x224 with align_corners=False; subtract minimum; divide by max clamped to >=1e-8

perturbations_in_order: contrast increase x1.05 about the per-channel spatial mean
circular spatial roll: +2 pixels vertically and -2 pixels horizontally
saliency_reliability.perturbation_domain: raw [0,1] tensor before ImageNet normalization; clamp to [0,1] after perturbation
saliency_reliability.similarity: cosine similarity between flattened base and perturbed Grad-CAM maps
saliency_reliability.degenerate_rule: if either map L2 norm <1e-10, similarity=0.0
saliency_reliability.aggregation: arithmetic mean of four similarities, clipped to [0,1]
saliency_reliability.published_cache_rng_note: v7.3.1 did not explicitly reseed PyTorch immediately before feature-cache generation; exact reported Q_S values are preserved in released feature caches
saliency_reliability.revision_code_rng: v7.3.2 explicitly sets Python, NumPy, and PyTorch seed to 42 before recomputation

seeds.training: Python random, NumPy, torch.manual_seed; CUDA seed if available
seeds.feature_test_sampling: np.random.default_rng(42); final paper used all held-out test images

tile_selection.grid_shape: rows=ceil(original_height/64), cols=ceil(original_width/64); therefore image-dependent, not a fixed 8x8 grid
tile_selection.boundary_rule: last row/column tiles are clipped with min(image_extent, start+64) and may be smaller than 64x64
tile_selection.priority_map_to_native_image: clip to [0,1], quantize to uint8, resize from 224x224 to original W x H using PIL bilinear interpolation, divide by 255
tile_selection.tile_score: mean resized reliability-weighted saliency over the native tile
tile_selection.tie_rule: Python stable sort preserves the original row-major tile order; exact ties therefore resolve by ascending tile ID
tile_selection.budget_boundary_note: rho is implemented as a tile-count fraction; because boundary tiles can be smaller, exact protected pixel area may differ slightly from rho
